caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1022 of 2022
lawyer:
Mr. Munshi Moniruzzaman, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Hasina Akhter, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner 
Mr. Sayed Ahmed, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md.Azim Uddin, Advocate -on-Record. -------- For the Respondent No.03 
Respondent Nos. 1, 2, 4 and 5 --------- Not represented
parties:
Advocate Razia Khatun ------ Petitioner
-Vs-
The State and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J. This Criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.03.2018 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous case No .39270 of 2015 disposing of the Rule with observations and directions. 

 2. Prosecution case, in brief, is that one Advocate Razia khatun, wife of Dr. Md. Akhtaruzzaman, Dhaka Bar Association, Dhaka, And, Publisher of the Book title, "concept and Laws on Alternative Dispute Resolution and Legal Aid" as informant lodged the First information Report (hereinafter referred as FIR) on 19.03.2014 against the accused persons under sections 82/85/91 of the copy Right Act, 2000 before the officer -in-Charge of kotwali police Station CMP, Chattogram, alleging inter alia that , the informant -petitioner is the Publisher of the famous law book title "concept and Law on Alternative Dispute resolution and Legal Aid" written by Dr. Md. Akteruzzaman, presently District Judge, Special Judge, Court No.5 who upon information from secret source, came to know that, the above named book has been pirated by someone, Upon further information from secret source, the informant -petitioner further gathered knowledge that, one business concern, namely, "Book collection" is doing copy, and, by publishing of the said book, selling the same illegally in the market. Accordingly, the informant-petitioner was able to collect the copy of pirated. Hence, Kotoali Police Station Case No. 451162, dated 18.03.2014 corresponding to G.R case No.162/2014 under sections 82/85/91 of the copy Right Act, 2000 was started against the accused -persons. Hence this case. 

 3. The Investigating officer took up the case for investigation. During investigation, the investigating officer collected the materials on record, recorded the statement of witnesses and after completing the investigation, submitted charge-sheet being charge-sheet No.313 dated 06.07.2014 before the chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chattogram against the accused persons as respondent Nos.2-5 herein under sections 82/85/91 of the copy Right Act, 2000. 

 4. After submission of charge-sheet, the case record was transferred to the court of Metro Sessions Judge, Chattogram who took cognizance of the case against the accused persons, and, transferred the case record to the court of Metro Additional Sessions Judge 3rd court, Chattogram for trail. 

 6. Subsequently, the informant- petitioner filed an application under section 526 of the code of criminal procedure, 1898 being Criminal Miscellaneous case. No.39270 of 2015 before the High Court Division for transfer of Sessions Case No.1635 of 2015 arising out of kotoali police station case No.45/162, dated, 18.03.2014 corresponding to G.R case No.162/2014 under sections 82/85/91 of the copy Right Act, 2000 pending in the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chattogram and obtained Rule, and, direction. 

 8. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 06.03.2018 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous case No.39270 of 2015, the informant as petitioner herein preferred the criminal petition for Leave to Appeal No.1022 of 2022 before this Division. 

 9. Mr. Munshi Moniruzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that, the High Court Division failed to grasp the essence of the application made under Section 526 of the code of Criminal procedure, and without considering the grave consequences that, may occur if the case is not transferred to another district erred in disposing of the Rule. He further submits that, the High Court Division failed to apply judicial mind in passing the impugned judgment and order inasmuch as the High Court Division failed to consider that, the case is pending from 2014, and it is denied to see daylight since then, due to the error of filing in the wrong and disfavourable jurisdiction. He next submits that, the High Court Division erred in law, and, in facts in passing the impugned judgment and order inasmuch as that, if failed to consider that, the accused respondents are local lawyers of the chattogram Bar who would apply all their power, and, influences to affect the outcome of the case, and, the informant petitioner being a woman would have no control in such matter which would cause miscarriage of justice. He also submits that, the High Court Division failed to apply judicial mind in passing the impugned judgment and order inasmuch as that, giving police protection only at the time of appearing in the court would not give proper protection to the informant petitioner, and, her life will continue to be in danger on the way to and from Dhaka, and, at all other times beyond that. He finally submits that, the High Court Division failed to consider that, out of four accused persons, three accused are the permanent residents from chattogram, and, one of them is a practicing Advocate of Chattogram Bar Association who have enough power in all respects i.e. family to friends, and other surroundings , but on the other hand, the informant-petitioner, and her family does not hold a minimum capacity to protect any untoward incident took place by the accused persons, and, mere police protection will not suffice, but, the High Court Division erred in law in disposing of the Rule without considering the said aspect, and such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 12. In the instant case, the petitioner i.e. the informant is a lady and learned Advocate of the Dhaka District Bar Association and the All of the accused are male and one of them is a number of the Chattogram District Bar Association, as such, we opine that fair and impartial inquiry or trail cannot be held without unwanted interruptions in any of the Dhaka and Chattogram Sessions Division. Moreover, some question of security and convenience and of unusual difficulty is likely to arise if the trail be held in those Jurisdictions. At the same time transfer will tend to the general convenience of the parties and witnesses and such an order is expedient for the ends of justice. 

 13. For that reasons, our considered view is that it will be beneficial for both of the parties if an order be passed to transfer the case to the Naryanganj Sessions Division which is between Dhaka and Chattogram Sessions Division and situated in a juncture for the purpose of transport facilities from both Dhaka and Chattogram District. 

 17. Accordingly, this petition is dis-posed of with stay. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. The learned Sessions Judge, 3rd court, Chattogram is directed to transmit the case record to the learned sessions Judge, Narayanganj within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of this order. 

 18. The learned Sessions Judge Narayanganj is further directed on getting the record of the case may start the, trail or transferred the case any competent court for trail. However, the concern court is at liberty to start the case as and when, if that stay order is vacated which is passed under section 561A of the code of Criminal procedure by the High Court Division.
